alignments.note: Passive verb with its subject pronoun, auxiliary and phrasal particle; the head stays on the lexical verb (rules 17 and 44).
The italic *of men* supplies both a preposition and a head noun the Hebrew never writes (rule 33's closing sentence); the italic corroborates without deciding (rule 7).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
One preposition whose scope is distributed across *after them* and *after a thief*; both English occurrences belong to it (rule 25), headed on the first.
The assimilated article is a real token, and the ASV writes *a thief* rather than *the thief*, so it takes nothing (rules 12 and 29).
Noun with the indefinite article English licenses (rule 15).

review_notes: The second *after* is read as the distributed scope of עָלֵימוֹ (rule 25) rather than as part of the comparative particle's rendering; giving it to כְּ was the competing reading.
*of men* is `added` because both the preposition and the noun are supplied; גֵּו itself is rendered by *midst*.
